extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (colleges, universities, school districts) and their Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for conducting Title IX grievance processes at recipients of federal education funding, covering evidence handling, investigator/decision-maker duties, training, impartiality, and procedural protections for parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written determination must state evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers must "lay out the evidentiary basis for conclusions reached in the case, in a written determination regarding responsibility." (§106.45(b)(7)(ii) language referenced)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies whether a single decision-maker or multiple decision-makers (hearing board) render the determination; the written determination should explain the evidence supporting conclusions so parties can understand the basis of the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' access to evidence and investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a determination, the recipient must make all evidence directly related to the allegations available to the parties for their inspection and review (§106.45(b)(5)(vi)) and "create an investigative report that fairly summarizes all relevant evidence" (§106.45(b)(5)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence subject to inspection must include both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence whether obtained from a party or another source. Parties may inspect/review evidence and the investigative report and have opportunity to identify and challenge perceived deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inculpatory and exculpatory evidence must be included
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations add language stating that evidence subject to inspection and review must include "inculpatory and exculpatory evidence whether obtained from a party or from another source."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients/investigators cannot withhold evidence favorable to either party; both types must be made available for inspection and consideration by parties and decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege-protected information excluded from evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules add §106.45(b)(1)(x), precluding the recipient from using evidence that would result in disclosure of information protected by a legally recognized privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence that would force disclosure of privileged communications may not be used, even if relevant; recipients should identify and exclude privilege-protected material from what is provided or relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator's obligation to gather evidence directly related to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are "obligated to gather evidence directly related to the allegations whether or not the recipient intends to rely on such evidence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators decide what is relevant (after considering parties' responses) and must gather and make available evidence directly related to the allegations regardless of their view of credibility or whether the recipient will rely on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigative report must "fairly summarize all relevant evidence" (§106.45(b)(5)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators must summarize evidence they deem relevant; parties have equal opportunity to review and respond to that report (including challenging relevance determinations) in writing and at any hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' right to inspect, review, and respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to inspect and review evidence directly related to the allegations and to review and respond to the investigative report, including making written arguments about relevance under §106.45(b)(5)(vii) and arguing relevance/persuasiveness at hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural opportunity to contest evidence/relevance before a decision is reached; responses can be considered by investigators and decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are "obligated to objectively evaluate all relevant evidence," and the parties may argue about relevance and persuasiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective evaluation requirement supports fair process; failure to objectively evaluate could be a ground for appeal (procedural irregularity). Decision-makers must consider inculpatory and exculpatory evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bias and conflicts of interest for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) prohibits bias and conflicts of interest and requires Title IX personnel to be free from such bias or conflicts when administering the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure investigators, decision-makers, Title IX Coordinators, and informal resolution facilitators serve without bias or conflicts; Department leaves recipients discretion on implementation (e.g., reporting/recusal mechanisms), but will hold recipients accountable for outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training on serving impartially (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training is required in "how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias." (§106.45(b)(1)(iii) revised language)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must focus on impartiality, avoiding prejudgment, COI, and bias. The Department interprets training to include the definition of sexual harassment in §106.30. Recipients have flexibility on frequency and additional content but must ensure personnel are trained when serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for decision-makers on hearing procedures, technology, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers must receive training "in how to conduct a grievance process including how to use technology that will be used by a recipient to conduct a live hearing, and on issues of the relevance of questions and evidence (including how to determine the relevance or irrelevance of a complainant's prior sexual history)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should prepare decision-makers to run hearings (including live, technology-enabled hearings) and to make relevance determinations about questions/evidence, including sensitive topics like prior sexual history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for investigators on issues of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must receive training on issues of relevance to prepare an investigative report that fairly summarizes relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should cover how to identify and evaluate relevant evidence and how to document and summarize relevant factual findings in the investigative report; parties' responses should be considered in relevance determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials must not rely on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations prohibit training materials that "rely on sex stereotypes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to provide an exhaustive definition of "sex stereotypes," but requires that training materials must not rely on such stereotypes. This prohibition does not bar evidence-based or peer-reviewed research about sexual violence dynamics (e.g., trauma impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency requirement for training materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Training materials referred to in §106.45(b)(1)(iii) "must be made publicly available on a recipient's website, or if the recipient does not have a website such materials must be made available upon request for inspection by members of the public." (§106.45(b)(10)(i)(D) revision)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure of training materials (including audio/video when used) is intended to facilitate oversight and reduce biased training; recipients should post or make materials inspectable to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for recipients to use employees or outsource
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department leaves recipients discretion to use their own employees or to outsource Title IX investigation and adjudication functions; it declines to require external, unaffiliated personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may choose internal staff or external contractors but must ensure compliance with impartiality and training requirements. The Department encourages best practices (e.g., institutional independence for investigators) but will not prescribe employment-relationship rules per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for evaluating alleged bias: objective/reasonable-person approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether bias exists "requires examination of the particular facts of a situation" and the Department encourages recipients to apply an objective (whether a reasonable person would believe bias exists), common-sense approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to adopt an "appearance of bias" standard or specify per se disqualifying professional experiences; recipients should avoid broad generalizations and examine facts, bearing in mind mandatory training is intended to mitigate bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal appeal rights for both parties, including on bias/COI and procedural irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations provide the parties equal appeal rights including on the ground of procedural irregularity, which could include a recipient's failure to objectively evaluate all relevant evidence or that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias that affected the outcome. (§106.45(b)(8) referenced)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal procedures must be symmetric and allow claims that bias/COI or other procedural irregularities affected the outcome; recipients should structure appeals to permit such challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators are not required to identify data gaps in investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not require investigators to identify data gaps in the investigative report, because parties' rights to inspect and review evidence and to respond to the report provide opportunity to identify perceived data gaps and challenge deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative reports should summarize relevant evidence; parties can point out perceived gaps in their responses or at hearings rather than relying on investigators to flag every gap.
